findings.claim: The plan runs the git check only on sources entries that `git ls-files` lists as written, so it treats every entry as a repo-root path. OKF section 6.2 defines path-valued resources as a bundle-relative path starting with `/` (from the bundle root) or a path relative to the concept. Under the plan's rule, a spec-form entry such as `/decisions/0006-x.md` or `../manifesto.md` never matches `git ls-files`. It gets reported as 'source not found', and changes to that file are never noticed. Sources that point at another concept, which section 5.1 names as the lineage case, fail the same way. The spike does not settle this: its sample had 0 spec-form paths and 0 concept sources, and its README says so. Its own finding is that the real bundle uses non-spec repo-root paths. That breaks I4 ('reads OKF as it is'). The fix is to resolve the entry as section 6.2 says (bundle root for `/`, the concept's directory otherwise), then check the resolved repository path against `git ls-files`. Whether to also accept bare repo-root paths, which real bundles use, is a contract choice the plan must state.

The plan gives 'source not found' as a reason a concept is due. Section 5.1 lets a resource be a scope descriptor (free text such as 'all queries in BigQuery project X'), and that is valid OKF, not a broken source. Treated as a due reason, such a concept stays due for good: a new verified entry cannot clear it, so review due and the CI action report it on every run. The plan has to say whether an unresolvable entry is a due reason or a separate notice that verifying can clear or that does not count as due. Otherwise it changes what 'due' means beyond ADR 0006's three reasons.

Sources are now resolved per OKF section 6.2: URL skipped, '/' from the bundle root, relative from the concept folder with a repository-root fallback (backed by spike:review-due/1), and concept ids to the concept file.
An unresolved source, such as a scope descriptor, is now a separate 'source not resolved' notice and not a due reason, so verifying is no longer blocked by it.

Handoffs are concepts in .okf/handoffs/ (ADR 0008) that kmctl writes with stale_after but no verified entry. The plan runs the concept checks over every concept in .okf/ and lists expired handoffs separately, without saying handoffs are left out of the concept checks. As written, every handoff is due for 'no verified entry' from the moment it is written, and an expired one shows twice. The plan must say whether .okf/handoffs/ is excluded from the three concept reasons (and test it).
Sources are resolved per OKF section 6.2 with a repository-root fallback backed by spike:review-due/1, and concept ids resolve to the concept file.
An unresolved source is a separate 'source not resolved' notice, not a due reason.

The plan now leaves .okf/handoffs/ out of the three concept checks, lists only expired handoffs with the 'passed' function shared with handoffs-list, never treats index.md or log.md as concepts, and the done-when adds a test that a handoff is neither due for lacking verified nor listed twice.

A tracked source whose path has non-ASCII characters never resolves, so its change is missed and it is reported as 'source not resolved'. `git ls-files` quotes such paths by default (core.quotePath), e.g. "src/caf\303\251.py", and the set lookup never matches. Use `git ls-files -z` and split on NUL, with a test.
has_passed treats stale_after as passed only when it is strictly before now, but OKF 5.5 says a concept is stale when now >= stale_after. At the exact instant a concept is not reported due.

A directory source such as 'src/pkg' is never a tracked file, so it becomes a 'source not resolved' notice even though `git log -- src/pkg` would give its last change. This matches the plan's wording but makes a common source form unusable.
test_exit_and_json never asserts that the fixture is actually due, so r7's 'nonzero when concepts are due' could pass on a fixture with nothing due. It also does not check the --json exit code.

entries.change: git ls-files runs with -z and splits on NUL so non-ASCII paths match, and a source that names a tracked folder resolves so git log -- folder dates it.
has_passed is true at or after stale_after (now >= stale_after), per OKF 5.5, with the docstring updated.
Tests for a non-ASCII source name and a folder source; the r7 test now checks the fixture is due and that --json exits 0.
A test that has_passed is true at the exact stale_after instant and false one second before.

findings.claim: Non-ASCII source paths now resolve; ls-files -z is split on NUL.
has_passed is now now >= stale_after, per OKF 5.5.
A source naming a tracked folder now resolves and is dated by git log.
test_exit_and_json now asserts the fixture is due and checks the --json exit code.

The review due help text still says a source that resolves to no tracked file becomes a notice. Since f3, a tracked folder also resolves, so the help should say 'no tracked file or folder'. Agents read this help to know which source forms work.

entries.change: The review due epilog now says a source resolving to no tracked file or folder is a notice.
